subfield: Astrophysics and cosmology (radio astronomy, fundamental physics probes)
motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes found a millisecond radio burst in archival Parkes data whose dispersion measure far exceeded the Milky Way's contribution, identifying a new extragalactic phenomenon: fast radio bursts. Their detection founded a field. Thousands of FRBs are now known, host galaxies have been localised, and a Galactic magnetar source has been identified. FRBs have become precision probes of fundamental physics. Their dispersion measures have located the 'missing' cosmic baryons in the intergalactic medium, and they are used to constrain the Hubble constant, the photon mass, the equivalence principle, the distance-duality relation and compact dark matter. This single serendipitous, carefully verified discovery opened a new window on the Universe. It is central to the science programmes of CHIME, ASKAP, MeerKAT and the SKA.
